protected_behaviors.behavior: The existing MAP -> FOCUS -> GATE -> RESOLVE -> APPROVAL -> STAGED decision tree remains the tutorial; no separate product tour replaces it.
EXPLORE remains reserved for genuine exploration; ordinary selection/focus/decision actions use truthful verbs.
Brand/title and canonical Home action return through the existing Atlas Home owner; no second navigation state machine is created.
Search, filters, selection, and other orthogonal state survive unrelated scene transitions and visibility changes.
Blocked/protected states remain visibly blocked and never gain an inviting reclaim/delete affordance.
The accepted warm material / Memory Atlas visual world is preserved during refinement; bounded implementation may not silently reset the product into a generic dashboard.
Contextual reticle/custom pointer remains scoped to the Atlas interaction region and supported pointer/motion conditions.
Cross-input semantics remain one capability model with pointer/keyboard/touch adapters; no second mobile state machine.
Every operable action produces a scene/context transition, named impact, feedback/readback, and continuation; dead clicks are regressions.
Technical safety facts are resolved by deterministic adapters/reducers before HUMAN_REVIEW; the operator is not asked to guess ownership, serviceability, repository uniqueness, or regenerability.
Human judgment is limited to value/preference and exact destructive authorization after technical safety resolution.
Classification and decisions persist into filterable views/queues and remain available after returning Home.
Motion communicates state/progress/transition only; decorative choreography must not obscure or delay task completion.
Static HTML/unit proof cannot close a live UX claim; supported viewport/input modes require bounded live proof.
Deleting, weakening, or rewriting a test/fixture to fit a broken candidate does not count as a repair; accepted behavior remains the oracle unless explicit redesign authority changes it.

A whole LocalAppData application directory cannot become reclaimable from path/age/size/cache heuristics when Windows installation or serviceability metadata intersects that tree; the UI must resolve app ownership first and offer semantic repair/uninstall choices rather than raw delete.

FileSteward represents storage as potentially multi-owned. App, repo, worktree, toolchain, service/task, package, generated-output, and user-data relationships are resolved together; the most protective current edge wins.

Repository lifecycle labels are evidence-backed and user-legible: ACTIVE, STABLE, LEGACY_CANDIDATE, and GENERATED_OUTPUT are distinct. Entire may enrich activity/change-impact evidence, but age, inactivity, or absence from Entire can never by itself create LEGACY_CANDIDATE or delete eligibility.

Transient context stays local to its pointer or keyboard anchor, never covers the hovered subject, related visible evidence or active controls, and fails to compact or suppressed context rather than remote docking. Unavailable targets keep the native pointer and no action promise.

Visible operable control changes no canonical context, impact, or continuation.
Unknown or non-exploratory action is rendered as EXPLORE.
Opening/closing a gate or toggling visibility clears active search/filter/selection without user intent.
New scene adds a separate Home/router state owner instead of existing Atlas Home authority.
Bounded feature work replaces accepted Memory Atlas material/interaction language with generic dashboard styling.
Agent declares cross-viewport/input UX complete from static/unit checks alone.
Local agent invents a question, choice, scene, or action because canonical judgment is missing.
UI asks user whether bytes are safe/regenerable/app-owned/repo-unique before safe adapters are exhausted.
Value decision or authorization appears before current attribution/consequence/recoverability gates are satisfied.

Candidate is %LOCALAPPDATA%\\VendorApp and Windows uninstall metadata references an updater/uninstaller inside that tree, but FileSteward offers raw reclaim/delete because the directory is under AppData or appears inactive.

Windows still reports an application installed, but its registered Update.exe/uninstaller is missing after prior cleanup; FileSteward treats the remaining/broken tree or registration as an orphan eligible for deletion instead of protected APP_INSTALLATION_BROKEN/serviceability recovery.
A directory is classified only as repo content or only as app content even though another current owner/dependency edge exists; a less-protective classification wins and exposes reclaim.
Repo/file has no current Entire session/graph evidence and is marked legacy or reclaimable without clean/recoverable/no-unique-work/no-current-dependency proof.
Repo/file is labeled legacy from old timestamps or no recent commit despite unresolved worktree, remote, unique-work, dependency, or reproducibility state.
A tooltip is farther than 48 CSS pixels from its anchor or intersects hovered/related evidence or controls after placement/clamping.
Keyboard context follows old pointer coordinates, or scroll/resize/scene changes leave stale context visible.
A delayed Home explanation timeout hides a subsequently opened RESOLVE panel and displaces the guide under the Chamber.
A valid explicit FRAME RANGE drag loses its cue at the next animation frame because it has no element host.
A panel shrinks at its old viewport-edge position, then expands after collision solving and covers evidence or controls.

positive_controls.case: Selecting an unknown large directory preserves current search/filter state, enters FOCUS, then automatically routes to attribution checks.
Installed app serviceability bytes resolve to protected consequence; operator is offered KEEP/REVIEW_LATER, not raw delete.
Regenerable app cache proves recovery, offers CLEAN_CACHE, authorizes exact action, verifies measured reclaim, and returns to next decision.
Clean pushed reproducible repo clone is technically safe but remains an operator value decision before removal.
Post-action health regression routes to incident recovery and freezes same-family automatic eligibility until classified.

Windows reports an installed per-user app whose uninstall/update executable lives under its LocalAppData tree. FileSteward binds the directory to the app, protects raw deletion, and asks only whether the user wants to keep/repair the app or remove it through semantic uninstall recovery.

The registered updater/uninstaller path is missing while the app remains installed in Windows. FileSteward classifies APP_INSTALLATION_BROKEN, preserves the tree/registration from raw deletion, and routes to repair/reinstall or semantic uninstall recovery.

A path belongs to a clean repo but is also referenced by an installed application's runtime/toolchain path. The ownership graph shows both relationships and the application/shared dependency protection overrides repo-removal eligibility.

Entire Graph shows current working-tree relationship/change-impact evidence in a repo with an active worktree. FileSteward labels it Part of active repo and preserves it without requiring the user to interpret Entire output.

A repo is clean, remote-backed/recoverable, has no attached/current worktree, no unique local work, no current cross-domain dependency, and no current Entire activity evidence when Entire is available. FileSteward may label Legacy repo candidate but still leaves removal as an operator value decision.

A full explanation fits locally beside visible evidence; a crowded target falls back without covering evidence or promising unavailable exploration; keyboard focus anchors separately from physical reticle.
